newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras cuts national budget by 15 percent.
newsitem.headline: Honduras cuts national budget by 15 percent.

text.p: The government of Honduras has slashed the national budget for 1997 by about 15 percent in a bid to meet budget deficit goals, officials said on Tuesday.
The move, approved by President Carlos Roberto Reina during a cabinet meeting, will cut 1.949 billion lempiras from the budget, said Fernando Garcia, minister of Economy and Commerce.

Honduras' Congress approved a 12.998 billion lempira budget in December, forecasting that the resulting budget shortfall would be about three percent of GDP. The government has said it wants a budget deficit of below three percent of GDP.
"The government wants to reduce spending in order to have healthy finances and meet macroeconomic goals," Garcia said.

Cuts will be spread out among all government agencies and will target non-essential spending projects that can be delayed, Garcia said. ($1 = 12.76 lempiras) -- Gustavo Palencia, Tegucigalpa bureau, +504-266-3300
